title: Buyer problems & desired results
summary: Hospitality buyers need guests answered, arrival-ready, and extras offered without growing a 24/7 communications desk as fast as the portfolio. Named KPIs in Conduit stories are desired measures and company-attributed outcomes, not typical rates or promised results.
markdown:
## What this document means

This brief is about the work a hospitality buyer still has to get done and the result they would count as success. It is not a second catalog of [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals), or [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows). Those surfaces can sit inside a job; they are not the job.

A desired KPI (share of conversations closed without a person, minutes to reply, support FTE, ancillary revenue, NOI) is what an operator would watch. It is not a promised result for the next account. Named figures below are Conduit-attributed stories collected in [Customer evidence & usable proof](#knowledge/customer-evidence). Use one named customer per motion; do not average rates. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

Public FAQ copy says Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, with agents that answer messages and calls, handle routine requests, and coordinate with the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

## Work buyers need to accomplish

The recurring job is: keep every guest conversation answered with the right property and booking context, complete the stay (access, payments, extras), and grow units or nights without a matching night desk.

| Job | Situation | Workaround | Failure | Capability in the job | Change they would measure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cover threads without a night desk | After-hours calls, lockouts, late check-in | Call center, Google Voice, VA shifts | Hour waits; owner still in Slack | Agents on connected voice/chat/email/WhatsApp/OTA paths with available reservation context; confirm channel routing and supported actions per connector; escalate with history | First-response time; overnight hours covered; human issues per incident |
| One workspace for OTA + messaging + calls | Multi-channel STR or hotel | Two inboxes (e.g. Intercom + Hostaway) plus WhatsApp | Lost context; no performance view | Inbox with booking details beside the thread | Channels unified; time spent switching tools |
| Add units without linear guest-support hiring | 40→100+ listings or an acquisition | Hire per shift as volume climbs | Backlogs (e.g. 630 unread); model does not scale | Agents + workflows + knowledge teaching | Automation %; properties per support rep; hires avoided |
| Get guests arrival-ready without another app | Codes, deposits, waivers, extras | Email sequences, PDF guides, extra payment links | Guests still ask; access delayed | Portal: one branded stay link | Pre-arrival completion; inbound “how do I get in” volume |
| Offer extras in the live conversation | Unused rooms, gap nights, early check-in, spa | Pre-arrival upgrade emails | Independent-hotel page says those emails convert below 10% | Workflows/agents using booking rules | Ancillary attach—not a guaranteed lift |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

Agents answer using property information and reservation data, can create a task or update a booking through connected tools, and pass requests to the team. Inbox covers SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social, and connected OTA threads. Workflows send confirmations, check-in, follow-ups, and add-on offers the operator chooses. Portals give one stay link (no app) for details, checks, pay, upgrades, and the AI concierge. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox.md) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows.md) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals.md)

Segment flavor, not extra jobs: independent hotels want after-hours cover while the desk serves people in the lobby; hotel groups want shared brand standards with per-property policies; short-term rentals want listing-specific check-in and booking-change handling. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/short-term-rentals)

## Before and after workflows

**Scenario 1 — STR growth is a staffing problem.** Haven Vacation Rentals managed roughly 270 Smoky Mountain listings. Peak guest support was about 25 people across shifts. Conduit was already installed near 40% automation with few workflows; volume still scaled with units. After the team standardized answers and taught the system, the 2026 write-up reports 90% automation, two people per shift, 14 January listings without extra support hires, and scores held around 4.8–4.9. In a snowstorm with 90 same-day check-ins, three issues needed a human. That is Haven’s attributed path, not a template rate. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

HomeHop’s same job after a failed AI vendor and a Google Voice lockout: roughly 40 to 108 listings without extra guest-support hires, 70% automation, and voice coverage 1 AM–7 AM. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop)

**Scenario 2 — Boutique hotel as a hands-off asset.** The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel had cycled through Jurny’s PMS/call center and other hospitality call services: costs from $4,000 down to $1,200 a month, guests waiting up to an hour, the owner still answering Slack, refunds mounting. Desired result was investor-grade, low-touch operations. The story reports support at $600/month, average response 57 minutes to 2 minutes, NOI up at least $3,400/month from costs and fewer refunds, and an 8% cap-rate translation of that NOI into more than $500,000 of modeled asset value. The write-up describes an AI platform plus a 24/7 staffed support team, so the software-only contribution is not isolated. Cap-rate math is the owner’s model, not an appraisal. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

**Separate STR acquisition example — Cascadia Getaways.** The vacation-rental manager reports 60% automation and a 4.9 communication score across 100 properties. During acquisition integration, leadership expressed confidence about adding properties without extra guest-service hires; this is an expectation, not a completed staffing result or hotel proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways)

## How improvement would be measured

Pair each desired change with a source of truth. Do not treat a story number as an SLA.

| Desired change | Named, attributed examples | Not the same as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work closed without a person | Haven 40%→90%; HomeHop 70%; Canbnb 60% of ~1,500 msgs/week; Flex title 70% vs header 90% | A comparable denominator or product guarantee |
| Speed | Lauderdale 57 min→2 min avg; Wynwood resolution 14–15 min→3 min | Instant replies on every issue |
| Staffing / cost | Haven ~25→two per shift (page: no AI layoffs); Easy BnB ~$22k/month and 11 VAs replaced, reported on the Bali Luxury Stays page | The same layoff vs. no-layoff outcome everywhere |
| Quality while automating | Haven 4.8–4.9; Cascadia locked at 4.9 | Proof that reviews always rise |
| Revenue / asset | Cosmica ~5% of Dubai revenue from upsells/cross-sells at peak; Lauderdale NOI/cap math | Typical ancillary % |

[Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cosmica) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways)

Conduit’s agent FAQ says how much agents resolve depends on guest requests, knowledge base, integrations, and escalation rules, and to track resolved conversations and handoffs. Inbox FAQ says messaging automation depends on the requests and how agents are configured. Those are measurement instructions, not forecasts. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox.md)

## Turning problems into campaigns

Lead with the job, then one named proof, then the surface. Drafts must not invent a relationship or claim every customer shares the pain. Writing rules: [Campaign writing examples & rules](#knowledge/writing-examples), [Audience-to-message map](#knowledge/message-map).

- **Cannot hire as fast as units.** Haven or HomeHop; ask current automation %, overnight headcount, and whether policies live in one knowledge base. [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals).
- **Guests wait; owner still in Slack.** Lauderdale minutes and support cost; confirm call-center spend and refund leakage. [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels).
- **Two inboxes.** Bocobay left Intercom to unify WhatsApp, email, phone, and live chat. The page header “80% resolution” / “100s hours” is not derived in the body—do not lead with it. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay)
- **After hours is the real desk.** Independent-hotel after-hours language plus HomeHop 1–7 AM voice. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)
- **Money left on extras.** Workflows can offer early check-in, gap nights, and upgrades; Cosmica’s ~5% Dubai figure is one market’s peak. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/workflows.md)

This pack has no hotel-group P&L body, no isolated Portals outcome, and no shared automation denominator. Investigate those before writing group-wide guarantees. Capability mapping: [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities).
open_questions: What denominator (messages, support tickets, guest communication) should campaigns use when customer stories disagree, as on The Flex 70% vs 90%?
Which named hotel-group or multi-property hotel outcomes exist beyond Lauderdale and Wynwood, which is multi-market CX rather than group ops?
Do any named stories isolate Guest Portals (pre-arrival completion, deposits, in-portal upgrades) as the cause of a result?
How should staffing proof be framed when Haven reports no AI layoffs and Bali/Easy BnB reports eleven VAs replaced?

evidence_notes.statement: Conduit’s public FAQ defines the buyer as hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers whose agents answer messages and calls and coordinate with the team.
evidence_notes.quote: Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers. Its AI agents answer guest messages and calls, handle routine requests, and coordinate work with your team.

evidence_notes.statement: Agents are described as answering with property and reservation data, acting in connected tools, and handing off to the team.
evidence_notes.quote: An AI agent answers guest messages and calls using your property information and reservation data. It can also take actions through connected tools, such as creating a task or updating a booking, and pass requests to your team.

evidence_notes.statement: How much agents resolve is stated as dependent on requests, knowledge, integrations, and rules—not a fixed rate.
evidence_notes.quote: The share depends on your guest requests, knowledge base, integrations, and escalation rules. Track resolved conversations and handoffs to see what your agents can handle and where they need help.

evidence_notes.statement: Inbox is described as unifying SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social, and connected OTA threads.
evidence_notes.quote: Conduit brings SMS, WhatsApp, email, calls, social messages, and connected OTA threads into one workspace. You can organize them by team, property, or group.

evidence_notes.statement: Haven’s attributed staffing outcome is an 80% reduction in support staffing needs, from 25 people to two per shift.
evidence_notes.quote:
80 percent reduction in support staffing needs
—from 25 people to two per shift

evidence_notes.statement: Lauderdale’s attributed speed and cost outcomes are 57 minutes to 2 minutes average response and support costs from $4,000 to $600/month.
evidence_notes.quote:
Reduced support costs from $4,000 to $600/month
Increased NOI by at least $3,400/month through reduced costs, and significant fewer refunds
Improved average response time from 57 minutes to 2 minutes on average, and instantaneous responses for most issues.

evidence_notes.statement: HomeHop’s attributed growth outcome is 40 to 108 listings without additional guest-support hires and 70% automation.
evidence_notes.quote:
Grew portfolio from
40 to 108 listings
without hiring additional guest support staff
Achieved
70 percent automation
with a clear path to 24/7 autopilot

evidence_notes.statement: Workflows are described as able to send messages, run follow-ups, and offer early check-in, gap nights, and room upgrades.
evidence_notes.quote: Workflows can send guest messages, run follow-up campaigns, and offer add-ons such as early check-in, gap nights, and room upgrades. You choose the trigger, conditions, and actions.

use_when: Drafting ABM or sales copy around buyer jobs rather than product names
Matching a prospect’s current workaround to one named customer story
Choosing which KPI to ask for in discovery without treating it as a Conduit guarantee
decisions_supported: Which job to lead with (coverage, unification, scale without hiring, arrival-ready stays, ancillary offers)
Which named proof is in-bounds for that job
Whether a number is a desired measure versus an attributed story versus an SLA
do_not_infer: A typical automation rate, response-time SLA, or ancillary-revenue percentage for new accounts
That Guest Portals or Operations produced the named case-study outcomes
Hotel-group P&L results from STR or single-hotel stories
That every operator will reduce headcount the same way (Haven vs Bali staffing outcomes conflict in kind)

evidence_validation: Exact passages checked; interpretation and proposed policies require review.

editorial_reviews.reason: Resolve final audience review: optional urgency, hotel versus rental evidence, named-customer attribution, and conditional connector readiness.
